evidence.input:
const moveIds = [
"pro-chance-events-need-no-divine-intervention","con-extraordinary-evidence-is-offered","pro-comparative-evidence-over-miracle-testimony","pro-alien-story-tests-claim-specific-evidence","pro-memory-is-reconstructive","con-luke-investigated-named-witnesses","pro-gospels-are-anonymously-attributed","con-luke-ordinary-accuracy-supports-historical-care","pro-closing-truth-claims-require-different-tests","con-gospel-identity-has-internal-and-external-support","con-memory-retains-central-life-changing-events","pro-martyrdom-shows-conviction-not-truth","con-early-christian-costly-sincerity","pro-informed-religious-disagreement","con-peter-source-and-first-person-access","con-james-family-access-and-costly-belief","con-first-person-experience-differs-from-inherited-belief","pro-apollonius-parallel","con-hostile-sorcery-testimony","pro-mormon-witness-comparator","con-apollonius-evidence-is-later-and-interested","pro-fatima-mass-witness-comparator","con-joseph-smith-witnesses-and-character-disanalogy","pro-islamic-miracle-tradition-comparator","pro-ancient-redeemer-patterns","con-jewish-context-resists-pagan-borrowing","pro-resurrection-remains-faith-not-public-knowledge","con-mythic-parallels-can-express-fulfilled-hope","con-closing-evidence-supports-commitment"];
const reasons = [
"Shermer’s many-opportunities argument correctly challenges inference from rarity alone. Its unresolved comparison-class problem is an evidentiary limitation, not base-rate neglect, because he expressly foregrounds background frequency.",
"Vandeweghe directly claims his historical evidence meets the heightened standard, but his detour through allegedly extraordinary atheist beliefs leaves Shermer’s claim-specific testimonial comparison unanswered and diverts attention to unrelated propositions.",
"Shermer compares resurrection testimony with mortality experience and ordinary transmission error. His failure to quantify the particular witnesses’ reliability weakens application, but does not assume the conclusion or rely on ignorance.",
"The invented alien narrative cleanly shows that mundane accuracy need not validate an extraordinary addition. Its limited similarity to Vandeweghe’s multiple-witness case is an analogy weakness, not a catalog-defined fallacy.",
"Shermer identifies reconstructive memory as a sincere error mechanism. His lack of a case-specific account of Gospel alteration limits probative force, but neither equivocates nor treats missing proof as disproof.",
"Vandeweghe offers a concrete investigative-source chain through Luke, named informants, and convergent reports. Independence and actual interviews remain insufficiently established, yet those unsupported connectors are not themselves circular reasoning.",
"Shermer challenges traditional authorship by citing prevailing scholarship and proposed dates. Because scholarly status does not settle his claim without underlying evidence, appeal to authority is plausible but not established as his sole inference.",
"Vandeweghe infers broader historical care from Luke’s accurate ordinary details. The transfer to miracle reporting is under-supported, but the speech does not shift a term’s meaning or create an unprincipled exception.",
"Shermer distinguishes public facts, preferences, private experiences, and political choices. The framework needs a clearer test for singular history, yet this categorization problem does not satisfy equivocation or ambiguity-effect definitions.",
"Vandeweghe supplies internal linguistic fit and uniform external attribution for Gospel identities. Each indicator is contestable and underdeveloped, but citing manuscript and patristic evidence is not merely invoking institutional prestige.",
"Vandeweghe distinguishes stable central memories from fallible peripheral details. The three-month study does not establish decades-long supernatural interpretation, but that scope mismatch is ordinary overextension rather than scope neglect as defined.",
"Shermer’s counterexamples validly separate costly conviction from truth. They fit inherited belief better than alleged firsthand experience, but he acknowledges the general target and does not apply inconsistent standards.",
"Vandeweghe uses persecution and refusal to retract to support sincerity. His movement among witnesses, associates, and later Christians weakens access claims, but the frozen critique does not establish a meaning shift or scale-insensitive judgment.",
"Shermer treats informed Jewish nonconversion as evidence that Christian claims are not publicly compelling. Disagreement alone cannot settle evidential adequacy, but he also provides comparative reasoning, so argument from ignorance is not established.",
"Vandeweghe combines Peter’s asserted source connection, close access, ordinary knowledge, unflattering portrayal, and costly persistence. Several historical links are asserted, yet the cumulative inference does not simply presuppose miracle truth.",
"Vandeweghe argues that James’s family access, prior skepticism, later worship, and death make deception unlikely. Family knowledge does not establish every miracle, but this inferential gap is not a catalog-defined defect.",
"Vandeweghe directly distinguishes dying for inherited teaching from dying for alleged public adult experience. The distinction depends on disputed historical premises, but it is principled and therefore not special pleading.",
"Shermer uses Apollonius to challenge uniqueness through narrative resemblance. His initial failure to compare dating, source plurality, and witness access makes the analogy incomplete, but does not establish belief bias or equivalence by definition.",
"Vandeweghe moves from hostile sorcery language to claimed corroboration of real extraordinary activity. The text may attest accusation or reputation only, but this overreading does not clearly shift a stable term’s meaning.",
"Shermer presents signed Mormon witnesses as a structural challenge to Christian testimonial confidence. Calling the story crazy invites belief-based reaction, yet the actual inference relies on witness form rather than incredibility alone.",
"Vandeweghe answers Apollonius with later dating, single sourcing, interested commissioning, and fantastic content. These claimed differences are relevant and principled, though defeating one comparator does not independently prove Christianity.",
"Shermer compares Fatima’s reported crowd with resurrection witness claims to test consistency. Crowd size alone omits independence and perception details, but explicitly emphasizing scale is not scope neglect.",
"Vandeweghe cites spiritual sight, witness conflict, and Smith’s conduct to distinguish Mormon testimony. Character allegations do not resolve every witness, but they function as evidence rather than merely exploiting an unbelievable conclusion.",
"Shermer catalogs Islamic miracle reports and claimed attestations. His outsider claim that traditions are indistinguishable outruns the comparison, but the resulting weakness is unsupported equivalence rather than a defined catalog fallacy.",
"Shermer identifies recurring divine-son, resurrection, and redemption motifs. The absence of a demonstrated borrowing route limits historical force, but thematic comparison does not assume fabrication or treat uncertainty as proof.",
"Vandeweghe offers scriptural saturation and Jewish resistance to Hellenism against direct borrowing. The broad cultural characterization cannot exclude indirect influence, but this is incomplete evidence rather than special pleading.",
"Shermer separates ordinary facts about Jesus from resurrection and atonement, combining mortality base rates with informed disagreement. Nonacceptance does not prove falsity, but his conclusion is not based on ignorance alone.",
"Vandeweghe offers fulfilled human hope as an alternative interpretation of mythic parallels and invokes C. S. Lewis illustratively. The interpretation lacks independent support, but Lewis’s status is not presented as settling it.",
"Vandeweghe links claimed early historical evidence to rational commitment, then uses the hallway metaphor to urge choice. The metaphor adds no evidential weight, but it states a practical consequence rather than replacing the historical case."
];
const moveReviews=moveIds.map((moveId,i)=>({moveId,reason:reasons[i]}));
const candidateReviews=[
{moveId:"con-extraordinary-evidence-is-offered",type:"fallacy",label:"Red herring",decision:"accept",context:"Atheists also believe extraordinary claims about life, consciousness, and the universe, though those are not tonight’s issue.",rationale:"Vandeweghe explicitly turns from whether his historical miracle evidence meets Shermer’s comparative standard to unrelated atheist commitments, leaving the testimony-versus-error challenge insufficiently answered."},
{moveId:"pro-gospels-are-anonymously-attributed",type:"fallacy",label:"Appeal to authority",decision:"reject",rationale:"Shermer cites what most biblical scholars think without presenting their underlying evidence, but he also states authorship and dating claims directly; the frozen critique identifies under-support, not status treated as conclusive."},
{moveId:"con-luke-ordinary-accuracy-supports-historical-care",type:"fallacy",label:"Equivocation",decision:"reject",rationale:"Vandeweghe transfers confidence from accurate geography and voyage details to careful miracle reporting, but he does not change the meaning of a key word; the defect is insufficient cross-category support."},
{moveId:"pro-closing-truth-claims-require-different-tests",type:"bias",label:"Ambiguity effect",decision:"reject",rationale:"Shermer favors publicly checkable claims and treats private experiences cautiously, yet his taxonomy expressly recognizes uncertainty rather than rejecting resurrection merely because singular historical evidence is less clear."},
{moveId:"con-memory-retains-central-life-changing-events",type:"bias",label:"Scope neglect",decision:"reject",rationale:"Vandeweghe extrapolates a short retention study to much longer Gospel transmission, but he expressly discusses percentages, elapsed time, and central versus peripheral content rather than ignoring scale or magnitude."},
{moveId:"pro-informed-religious-disagreement",type:"fallacy",label:"Argument from ignorance",decision:"reject",rationale:"Shermer overstates what informed nonconversion proves, but he does not rely only on Christianity’s failure to compel assent; the move sits within positive comparative testimony and public-verification reasoning."},
{moveId:"con-first-person-experience-differs-from-inherited-belief",type:"fallacy",label:"Special pleading",decision:"reject",rationale:"Vandeweghe applies a different assessment to alleged disciples and later zealots, but supplies a principled distinction—claimed firsthand public adult experience versus inherited teaching—even though its historical premises remain disputed."},
{moveId:"pro-apollonius-parallel",type:"bias",label:"Confirmation bias",decision:"reject",rationale:"Shermer selects similarities that support a comparator and initially omits evidential differences, but the frozen critique shows an incomplete comparison, not selective handling of contrary information within the retained source."},
{moveId:"con-hostile-sorcery-testimony",type:"fallacy",label:"Equivocation",decision:"reject",rationale:"Vandeweghe reads sorcery language as conceding real supernatural power, while it could record accusation or reputation; that inference overreaches but does not demonstrably shift the term’s meaning mid-argument."},
{moveId:"pro-mormon-witness-comparator",type:"bias",label:"Belief bias",decision:"reject",rationale:"Shermer calls the Mormon narrative crazy, but his substantive comparator uses a signed group affidavit and detailed origin testimony; the inference is not based solely on the conclusion feeling unbelievable."},
{moveId:"con-apollonius-evidence-is-later-and-interested",type:"bias",label:"Confirmation bias",decision:"reject",rationale:"Vandeweghe stresses late, commissioned, fantastic Apollonius material favorable to his disanalogy, but the retained critique does not establish that he knowingly discounts contrary evidence rather than presenting an incomplete comparison."},
{moveId:"pro-fatima-mass-witness-comparator",type:"bias",label:"Scope neglect",decision:"reject",rationale:"Shermer emphasizes fifty thousand reported witnesses against five hundred, directly adjusting for numerical scale; his omission concerns witness quality and independence, not failure to notice magnitude."},
{moveId:"con-joseph-smith-witnesses-and-character-disanalogy",type:"bias",label:"Belief bias",decision:"reject",rationale:"Vandeweghe uses harsh character judgments, but supports them with alleged spiritual sight, witness conflict, and public-private inconsistency; the comparison is incomplete rather than decided only by an intuitively disreputable conclusion."},
{moveId:"pro-islamic-miracle-tradition-comparator",type:"fallacy",label:"Begging the question",decision:"reject",rationale:"Shermer’s claim that traditions are indistinguishable assumes more evidential parity than his catalogue demonstrates, yet it does not literally insert the conclusion into a premise; it remains an unsupported comparison."},
{moveId:"con-jewish-context-resists-pagan-borrowing",type:"fallacy",label:"Argument from ignorance",decision:"reject",rationale:"Vandeweghe says there is zero evidence of mythological influence, but also supplies positive cultural considerations about Hebrew-scripture saturation and resistance to pagan imagery, so absence of proof is not his sole basis."},
{moveId:"pro-resurrection-remains-faith-not-public-knowledge",type:"fallacy",label:"Argument from ignorance",decision:"reject",rationale:"Shermer invokes informed nonacceptance, but also relies on mortality background rates and comparative testimonial weakness; his conclusion is not simply that resurrection is false because it remains unproved."},
{moveId:"con-mythic-parallels-can-express-fulfilled-hope",type:"fallacy",label:"Appeal to authority",decision:"reject",rationale:"Vandeweghe cites C. S. Lewis and his conversion to illustrate a fulfilled-hope interpretation, but does not claim Lewis’s stature proves historicity; the real limitation is missing independent support."},
{moveId:"con-closing-evidence-supports-commitment",type:"fallacy",label:"Red herring",decision:"reject",rationale:"The hallway and commitment imagery does not strengthen disputed historical premises, but it presents the practical significance Vandeweghe draws from his retained evidence rather than abandoning the motion entirely."}
];
const acceptedTags=[{moveId:"con-extraordinary-evidence-is-offered",type:"fallacy",label:"Red herring",url:"https://logfall.com/fallacies/red-herring/",context:"Atheists also believe extraordinary claims about life, consciousness, and the universe, though those are not tonight’s issue.",rationale:"Vandeweghe explicitly turns from whether his historical miracle evidence meets Shermer’s comparative standard to unrelated atheist commitments, leaving the testimony-versus-error challenge insufficiently answered."}];
const obj={schemaVersion:"1.0-source-grounded-rhetorical-review",debateNumber:"288",debateId:"shermer-vandeweghe-jesus-miracles-2019",reviewedMoveIds:moveIds,moveReviews,candidateReviews,acceptedTags,audit:{completeSourceReviewed:true,allMovesReviewed:true,otherReviewerUnavailable:true,scoresUnavailable:true,sourceRestrictionsRespected:true,noScoreChanges:true}};
const json=JSON.stringify(obj,null,2)+"\n";
store("review288b_json",json); store("review288b_obj",obj);
text(JSON.stringify({bytes:json.length,moves:moveReviews.length,candidates:candidateReviews.length,accepted:acceptedTags.length}));
